[USER] User is interested in practical measures workplaces can take to make them more welcoming to employees with mental health challenges.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employers can provide mental health benefits such as access to a therapist, counseling services, or employee assistance programs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employers can promote mental wellness by encouraging employees to take mental health days or providing mindfulness or meditation programs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employers can offer flexible work arrangements, such as flexible schedules or remote work options for employees who may need to attend therapy or manage mental health challenges.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employers can provide training sessions that educate managers and employees about mental health conditions, stigma reduction, and mental health first aid.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employers can foster a culture of open communication where employees feel comfortable discussing mental health challenges with their supervisor or HR department without fear of discrimination or retaliation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employers can provide accommodations for employees with mental health conditions, such as private rooms, noise-canceling headphones, or additional breaks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Employers can take steps to reduce stigma and discrimination by promoting a culture of empathy, understanding, and support, including training, creating a positive workplace environment, and supporting diversity and inclusion initiatives.
